from_quote: By Art. i, Sec. 2, representatives and direct taxes shall be apportioned among the several states, &c.
rationale: Cites "Art. i, Sec. 2" (OCR "i" for "1") and quotes the opening words of this clause.
to_quote: Representatives and direct Taxes shall be apportioned among the several States

from_quote: same art. sect. 8, the congress shall have powers to lay and collect taxes, duties, &c. for the common defence and general welfare, but all duties, imposts and excises, shall be uniform throughout the United States
rationale: Cites "same art. sect. 8" (Article 1, Section 8) and quotes this clause, abridging its middle with "&c."
to_quote: The Congress shall have Power To lay and collect Taxes, Duties, Imposts and Excises, to pay the Debts and provide for the common Defence and general Welfare of the United States; but all Duties, Imposts and Excises shall be uniform throughout the United States

from_quote: By the first recited clause, direct taxes shall be apportioned on the states.
rationale: Refers back to "the first recited clause," the Art. 1, Sec. 2 apportionment of direct taxes quoted in the preceding paragraph.
to_quote: direct Taxes shall be apportioned among the several States

from_quote: the qualifications of the president are required only of the person to be elected president
rationale: Names the qualifications required of the President, which only this clause sets out.

from_quote: but he may serve as president
rationale: Says the vice-president "may serve as president," naming the provision for the office to devolve on the Vice President, which is this clause.

from_quote: But the congress may by law vest the appointment of such inferior officers as they think proper in the president alone, in the courts of law, or in the heads of the departments:
rationale: Cites "art. 2, sect. 2" and quotes the last part of this clause in quotation marks, adding "the" before "departments."
to_quote: but the Congress may by Law vest the Appointment of such inferior Officers, as they think proper, in the President alone, in the Courts of Law, or in the Heads of Departments

from_quote: By art. 3, sect. 2, the supreme court shall have appellate jurisdiction as to law and facts with such exceptions, &c.
rationale: Cites "art. 3, sect. 2" and reproduces, slightly abridged, this clause's grant of appellate jurisdiction "with such exceptions."
to_quote: the supreme Court shall have appellate Jurisdiction, both as to Law and Fact, with such Exceptions

from_quote: By article 6, the proposed constitution, and the laws of the United States, which shall be made in pursuance thereof; and all treaties made, or which shall be made under the authority of the United States, shall be the supreme law of the land ; and the judges in every state shall be bound thereby ; anything in the constitution or laws of any state to the contrary notwithstanding.
rationale: Cites "article 6" and reproduces this clause almost word for word, with "the proposed constitution" for "This Constitution."
to_quote: This Constitution, and the Laws of the United States which shall be made in Pursuance thereof; and all Treaties made, or which shall be made, under the Authority of the United States, shall be the supreme Law of the Land; and the Judges in every State shall be bound thereby, any Thing in the Constitution or Laws of any State to the Contrary notwithstanding.

from_quote: the laws of the United States which shall be ; made in pursuance of the federal constitution will be also supreme laws
rationale: Continues the discussion of the Article 6 clause quoted in the preceding paragraph, repeating its words "the laws of the United States which shall be made in pursuance."
to_quote: the Laws of the United States which shall be made in Pursuance thereof

from_quote: By the article before recited, treaties also made under the authority of the United States, shall be the supreme law
rationale: Refers to "the article before recited" (Article 6, quoted in FederalFarmer.4.4) and repeats its words on treaties made "under the authority of the United States."
to_quote: all Treaties made, or which shall be made, under the Authority of the United States, shall be the supreme Law of the Land

from_quote: The president and two-thirds of the senate will be empowered to make treaties
rationale: Names the treaty power of "the president and two-thirds of the senate," which is in this clause.
to_quote: to make Treaties, provided two thirds of the Senators present concur

from_quote: To make all laws which shall be necessary and proper for carrying into execution the foregoing powers, and all other powers vested by this constitution in the government of the United States, or in any department or officer thereof.
rationale: Quotes the clause verbatim in quotation marks, introduced as "a general clause in art. i, sect. 8" (OCR "i" for "1").
to_quote: To make all Laws which shall be necessary and proper for carrying into Execution the foregoing Powers, and all other Powers vested by this Constitution in the Government of the United States, or in any Department or Officer thereof.

from_quote: But the convention found it necessary to recognize or re-establish the benefits of that writ
rationale: Says the convention recognized "the benefits of that writ," the writ of habeas corpus named earlier in the paragraph, which only this clause provides for.

from_quote: and the jury trial in criminal cases
rationale: Says the convention recognized "the jury trial in criminal cases," which this clause provides.
to_quote: The Trial of all Crimes, except in Cases of Impeachment, shall be by Jury

from_quote: But the convention, by Art. I, Sect. 10, have put a sanction upon this part even of the state compacts.
rationale: Cites "Art. I, Sect. 10" for the bar on ex post facto laws by the states; that bar is in the first clause of the section.

from_quote: the 9th and loth Sections in Art. i, in the proposed constitution, are no more nor less, than a partial bill of rights

from_quote: the federal legislature shall never pass a bill of attainder, or expost facto law

from_quote: that no tax shall be laid on articles exported
